NoSecurityExtension and client-auth policy can affect certificate mapping, but Domain Admin impersonation still needs an exact connector and template, controlled AD requester with enrollment rights, issued certificate and domain-controller mapping that accepts it. Corrected the page; do not restore the old unconditional AD-admin edge.

exclusion_technique: Weaken an existing PCA Connector for AD certificate template in place
review_evidence: UpdateTemplate may weaken an authentication-capable template, but replacing its definition does not itself grant enrollment or a target AD identity. The old arbitrary-UPN claim is unsupported by AWS's subject/SAN rules. Need exact template state, AD requester/group, resulting certificate and domain-controller mapping before an AD-principal edge; no AWS IAM role edge is established by the API alone.

GetCluster names the exact Slurm secret ARN and GetSecretValue can disclose the shared scheduler key, but the key authenticates to Slurm, not AWS IAM. A role edge additionally needs private scheduler reachability, job execution, exact cluster-to-queue-to-node role joins and evidence that credentials are exposed to that job. The old account-wide pcs!* secret match and instance-profile naming inference are insufficient. AWS PCS cluster-secrets and Slurm REST authentication docs.

exclusion_technique: Create a Parallel Computing Service (PCS) compute node group with a passed instance profile
review_evidence: AWS PCS requires the selected instance-profile role to have an AWSPCS name or /aws-pcs/ path and pcs:RegisterComputeNodeGroupInstance. CreateComputeNodeGroup plus PassRole can launch nodes with that profile, but it does not give the IAM caller a Slurm login or a way to submit code; AWS job submission uses sbatch from a reachable login node. The collector does not join a controlled scheduler/login foothold, exact cluster/queue and node group, or launch readiness. Keep candidate rather than assert target-role execution; AWS PCS instance-profile, minimum-permission and run-job guides.

Partner Central CreateEngagementInvitation shares Engagement snapshots with another connected Partner account after acceptance. The recipient is a Partner application membership, not an IAM user/role, and the operation does not confer another AWS principal's IAM actions. Retain as Partner Central data-sharing persistence, outside principal-to-principal IAM escalation (HackTricks source section).

aps:PutResourcePolicy on an exact AMP workspace can name a controlled IAM principal and grant bounded Prometheus query/ingest APIs, not general workspace management. Require the exact source mutation grant, workspace/Region, target principal and effective recipient authorization, including cross-account identity allow where applicable (AWS AMP resource-policy announcement and IAM cross-account policy evaluation).

kafka:PutClusterPolicy can grant a named external IAM principal bounded cluster access. Require exact cluster/Region, IAM authentication and policy actions, recipient identity allow, VPC connectivity and intended Kafka data-plane grant; policy permission alone does not prove broker reachability or a broader IAM role (AWS MSK cross-account cluster-policy guide).

Q Business CreateDataAccessor can grant SearchRelevantContent to a supported registered ISV IAM role, but arbitrary external AWS principals are not eligible. Require eligible ISV role/tenant, application and index, resource policy, Identity Center assignment, user authorization and exact resulting action; do not infer usable access from CreateDataAccessor alone (AWS Q Business data-accessor guide).

After consortium approval, CreateMember makes a Fabric network member owned by the external account. Its peer/CA identity is scoped to that blockchain network, not an IAM role in the victim account; retention of network access is a bounded persistence effect (HackTricks Managed Blockchain persistence page).

mediaconnect:GrantFlowEntitlements can allow a selected AWS subscriber account to create a same-Region flow sourcing a transport-stream flow; entitlement is one-use and only bounded MediaConnect content access. Require exact flow/Region, enabled entitlement, controlled subscriber, recipient CreateFlow rights and a usable source; no IAM role takeover follows (AWS MediaConnect entitlement guide).

mediapackagev2:PutChannelPolicy on an exact channel can grant PutObject to a named IAM principal or IP-scoped wildcard principal. Original wildcard example is an IP-restricted ingest exposure, not anonymous AWS authority. Require exact channel ARN without /*, named recipient and cross-account identity allow for a principal edge, or keep the wildcard case as service exposure (AWS MediaPackage ingest authorization and policy ARN requirements).

CreateAccessor returns a BillingToken usable for AMB Ethereum/Polygon node API requests owned by the account. AWS documents that it authenticates those blockchain requests, not general IAM API calls or another IAM principal. Retain as service credential persistence (AWS AMB token access guide).

payment-cryptography:PutResourcePolicy on a primary key can grant a named external IAM role bounded cryptographic operations; the external role must also allow the action in its identity policy. Require exact key/Region, primary-key state, role/principal, matching recipient allow and action; key access is not general IAM role access (AWS Payment Cryptography resource-policy guide).

mediapackagev2:PutOriginEndpointPolicy can grant GetObject/GetHeadObject on one exact endpoint to a named IAM principal or anonymously via wildcard principal. Require exact endpoint ARN without /* and effective recipient authorization for an IAM edge; original wildcard case is public content exposure, not principal takeover (AWS MediaPackage origin authorization and policy ARN requirements).

ram:CreateResourceShare or AssociateResourceShare can share an exact Cloud WAN core network with another account or IAM principal. Require exact resource/share/principal, accepted invitation where required, live managed RAM permission, recipient attachment rights and network policy; the share gives bounded attachment authority, not general IAM actions or assured reachability (AWS RAM shareable resources and Cloud WAN sharing guide).

PassRole lets Pipes assume a role only for supported source, enrichment and target operations; a configured pipe neither yields role credentials nor arbitrary API execution. Exact downstream effect requires valid resource and event joins. AWS CreatePipe and EventBridge Pipes execution-role docs.

StartPipe accepts only a pipe name and resumes its fixed configuration; it does not return role credentials or permit arbitrary API execution as that role. A stopped pipe must have pending or attacker-producible events to cause any downstream effect. AWS StartPipe API docs.

exclusion_technique: Promote a controlled QuickSight user to ADMIN
review_evidence: UpdateUser can set ADMIN on an existing QuickSight user, but source control of that exact user and its login cannot be inferred from IAM permission. Need user-to-source identity mapping, active sign-in and namespace/account plus effective UpdateUser on that user. AWS UpdateUser docs; active RegisterUser self-IAM-user route covers a separate case.

AddRoleToDBCluster plus PassRole can associate an exact role with an existing Aurora cluster, but no general role session follows. A role edge needs the cluster engine, supported feature, role trust and effective permissions, database authentication, SQL privilege, and an exact integration operation that grants additional AWS authority; RDS AddRoleToDBCluster and Aurora integration docs.

AddRoleToDBInstance plus PassRole can associate a role with a supported available DB instance, but the source does not thereby obtain role credentials. Need exact instance/engine/feature, role trust and effective permissions, database login and SQL access to a supported integration before a bounded authority edge; RDS AddRoleToDBInstance docs.

exclusion_technique: Create an RDS Custom instance with a passed AWSRDSCustom instance profile
review_evidence: CreateDBInstance can choose an AWSRDSCustom instance profile under the documented name, trust and KMS constraints. The source still needs a supported host-access or code-execution path to obtain the EC2 role credentials. No exact profile-to-access foothold is collected, so creation plus PassRole alone is insufficient; RDS Custom documentation.

rds-db:connect can authenticate to a configured Aurora DB user only when IAM DB authentication and the engine user are ready, the resource ID matches and the endpoint is reachable. A role association or extension name alone does not prove an operation using that role. Need exact SQL rights, active associated role, configured integration and role-permitted AWS operation; RDS IAM DB auth and Aurora integration docs.

IAM database authentication gives a database session, not the full permissions of an RDS associated IAM role. Need an exact DB user and rds-db:connect resource, enabled IAM auth, reachability, SQL rights, active associated role and configured integration exposing an additional AWS action; RDS IAM DB auth docs.

GetSecretValue on the exact RDS-managed master secret may give a database login when decryption and network access also work, but not an IAM role session. Need exact secret-to-database and active-role joins plus configured integration, SQL rights and a role-permitted AWS operation; RDS managed master secret and Aurora integration docs.

ModifyDBCluster may reset a cluster master password when RDS does not manage it through Secrets Manager. Password control still needs database reachability or a supported Data API path and a usable SQL integration to exercise any associated role. Need exact cluster state, role, feature and added AWS operation; RDS ModifyDBCluster and Data API docs.

ModifyDBInstance may reset a non-Aurora instance master password when RDS is not managing it. This gives potential database access, not the associated IAM role session. Need exact instance state, network route, SQL integration, active associated role and role-permitted operation before an authority edge; RDS ModifyDBInstance docs.

GetClusterCredentials returns a short-lived password for a named Redshift database user, not STS credentials for the cluster IAM role. The user gains only recorded SQL grants; any AWS-backed SQL action needs separate database privilege and associated IAM role evidence. No general other-principal AWS role edge follows from this call. AWS IAM database authentication guide.

GetClusterCredentialsWithIAM derives a Redshift database identity from the caller and returns SQL credentials, not another IAM role's STS credentials. Database rights depend on that mapped user and its SQL grants. No full AWS role edge follows from the API alone. AWS Redshift IAM database authentication guide.

ModifyCluster master password changes a Redshift database login. A database superuser may gain SQL administration, but the operation neither issues STS credentials nor transfers the cluster's IAM roles to the caller. AWS-backed SQL integrations still require their own role, SQL privilege and action-specific proof. AWS Redshift role and ASSUMEROLE docs.

ModifyClusterIamRoles or UpdateNamespace plus iam:PassRole can associate an exact role with a Redshift warehouse, but association alone does not yield its credentials. A definite bounded AWS action needs the warehouse and role join, Redshift service trust, effective scoped grants, a database login with SQL and ASSUMEROLE rights, and a specific supported SQL integration/action. Preserve as a candidate for precise service-mediated authority, not a full role edge. AWS Redshift role and ASSUMEROLE docs.

Redshift Serverless GetCredentials returns a temporary password for the IAM-mapped database user, not credentials for the namespace's IAM role. Its rights are SQL grants and database-role mappings; a separate AWS-backed SQL operation would need exact authorization evidence. No full other-principal AWS role edge follows from token vending alone. AWS Redshift Serverless GetCredentials API.

exclusion_technique: Remove a certificate attribute mapping that a negative role-trust condition relies on
review_evidence: DeleteAttributeMapping or PutAttributeMapping can remove a mapped x509 tag from a profile, changing a role trust with a negative or IfExists condition. The route only works with a source-held valid certificate, enabled anchor/profile, exact listed role, and a trust statement where absence makes the condition true. Candidate for exact before/after mapping and trust/certificate join; a broad action grant is insufficient (AWS DeleteAttributeMapping API and Roles Anywhere trust model).

exclusion_technique: Remove the session-policy restriction of an IAM Roles Anywhere profile
review_evidence: UpdateProfile can remove or replace inline/managed session restrictions on a profile without changing its roleArns. Reaching the listed role also requires source possession of a valid private key/certificate, enabled matching anchor/profile, successful role trust, and proof the old policy withheld rights; the API grant alone cannot show those facts. Candidate for exact profile/certificate/effective-rights join (AWS UpdateProfile API).

CreateWorkspaceServiceAccountToken alone can mint a bearer token for a known existing ADMIN Grafana service account. The active catalog route requires both CreateWorkspaceServiceAccount and token creation, so this narrower path is missing. Need exact service account ID and recorded ADMIN role, eligible workspace, effective token permission and endpoint access before a definite Grafana authority edge; this is not IAM role credentials. AWS token API.

AddPermission grants a caller or service bounded invoke access to an existing function; it does not itself expose the function role. A principal edge requires an exact target whose existing code lets that caller obtain role credentials or perform a role-permitted privileged operation. Function ARN, policy effect and executable behavior are not joined. Candidate for a concrete consumer path.

Exposing an existing NONE-auth function URL makes its current behavior callable publicly, but URL reachability is not Lambda execution-role credential access. Need an exact function URL, effective Create/Update URL and permission grants, and code behavior that yields a new IAM capability. Candidate; do not infer full role access from the URL setting.

AddLayerVersionPermission shares a layer version; it does not itself grant the layer publisher or any function execution role. A role pivot would require safely inspecting that exact layer version for usable AWS credentials or proving a downstream function imports controlled code. Neither follows from policy permission. Candidate for content or consumer evidence.

GetFunction returns deployment package access, but the package may contain no credentials and the API does not grant the execution role. Only a reviewed usable credential with an exact IAM subject and added authority could form a principal edge. Candidate for safe package-content inspection, not a generic role edge.

GetFunctionConfiguration may return plaintext environment values or secret references, but a role edge needs an actual usable AWS credential, its exact subject and added authority. The active aws-lambda-getconfig-secret-identity models that strict subset with content proof; this broad retired claim remains a candidate, not a full replacement.

GetLayerVersion lets a caller download one layer package, not assume a function role. A principal edge needs safe inspection of that exact package for a usable AWS credential and its added authority; shared code alone is data access. Candidate for credential-content evidence.

CreateTemplateGroupAccessControlEntry can allow an AD group to enroll, but no certificate or stronger AD identity follows from the entry alone. Need exact template and group SID, proof the source controls an eligible AD requester, a working enrollment path, an issued authentication certificate and mapping to a different principal. It does not grant an AWS IAM role; AWS Connector for AD group enrollment docs.

ApplySecurityGroupsToClientVpnTargetNetwork changes the network identity of a Client VPN association. Even when downstream security groups trust it, the source obtains no AWS IAM role or separate principal permissions; accepted client identity and application access are separate. This is a network authorization finding, not a principal-to-principal edge.

Associating a Client VPN subnet and adding a route can extend network reachability, subject to client authentication, endpoint authorization and downstream controls. These actions do not assign or expose another AWS IAM principal; keep the path in network exposure analysis.

AuthorizeClientVpnIngress broadens which destination network an already authenticated VPN client may reach. It neither creates an AWS IAM principal nor grants the caller a role session; an AWS identity pivot would require a separate service-specific exploit or credential.

GetVpnConnectionDeviceSampleConfiguration can disclose Site-to-Site VPN PSKs for Standard storage. A PSK authenticates a VPN peer, not an AWS IAM principal; tunnel operation additionally needs gateway and routing control. Keep as credential and network exposure, not IAM escalation.

ModifyClientVpnEndpoint can change DNS, routing behavior and connection logging, but it does not grant another AWS principal's IAM actions. Client authentication, endpoint routes and downstream application access remain separate; this is traffic manipulation and telemetry loss.

ModifyVpnConnection and ModifyVpnTunnelOptions can redirect or disable a Site-to-Site VPN peer with the gateway and tunnel prerequisites. They change network connectivity and PSKs, not an AWS role trust or credential. Keep as a network-plane takeover finding.

The source uses Timestream Select or Unload to read rows or export them to S3. This may expose table data but does not issue AWS role credentials, create an IAM grant, or move the caller to another principal; retain as bounded data access (HackTricks Timestream post-exploitation page).

The source uses Timestream Select or Unload to read rows or export them to S3. This may expose table data but does not issue AWS role credentials, create an IAM grant, or move the caller to another principal; retain as bounded data access (HackTricks Timestream post-exploitation page).

GetOidcInfo can disclose the Wickr OIDC client secret and optional IdP-flow tokens. Use still depends on the IdP OAuth flow; no AWS IAM role session or IAM policy grant follows from the read. Retain as integration-secret disclosure (HackTricks Wickr post-exploitation page; AWS GetOidcInfo API).

GetOpentdfConfig can disclose OpenTDF client credentials for a Wickr network. Those authenticate to the OpenTDF integration, not an AWS IAM principal; retain as application/integration-secret disclosure (HackTricks Wickr post-exploitation page; AWS GetOpentdfConfig API).

ListUsers may reveal a pending Wickr invitation enrollment code. That could help claim a Wickr user identity, but no exact IAM role, STS credential or IAM permission grant is identified. Retain as Wickr account takeover risk (HackTricks Wickr post-exploitation page; AWS ListUsers API).

GetDataAccess returns an STS session constrained by the Access Grants session policy to the granted S3 prefix; reaching the passed IAM role's full permissions is false. The active aws-s3-accessgrants-self-grant replacement models only a reviewed, newly effective GetObject permission for the exact source and prefix. Keep the broader role-target route as a candidate only if another effect beyond that bounded session is proven; AWS S3 Access Grants GetDataAccess guide.
Page/exclusion describe bounded S3 or Lambda job effects, not general passed-role credentials; verify possible exact principal gain.

exclusion_technique: Race-replace CloudFormation templates uploaded to a template bucket
review_evidence: PutObject on a CloudFormation template can affect a later deployment only if the exact object is fetched after the write by a known stack operation under a known execution role. Bucket naming and PutBucketNotification alone do not prove that consumer or timing. The current collector lacks object-to-stack/role use and version linkage; candidate pending an exact artifact consumer witness.

exclusion_technique: Replace an S3 object fetched and run by an EC2 managed node
review_evidence: Writing an S3 object gives an EC2 role only if a known instance bootstrap actually fetches and executes that exact object after the write. Native EC2 user data is stored on the instance and does not inherently reference S3. The collector lacks a recorded bootstrap command/object version and its exact instance-profile join; candidate pending those facts. AWS EC2 user data guide.

exclusion_technique: Tamper with a Terraform state file consumed by a pipeline
review_evidence: Changing a Terraform state object affects a later pipeline only if that exact state key is read by a known apply job under a known IAM role and the edited state can cause a privileged action. A .tfstate-looking key and S3 write are insufficient. The collector has no state-backend, pending apply, plan-effect or pipeline-role join; candidate pending those concrete facts.

AWS CreateFileSystem requires a bucket/prefix and service role with access to that bucket; the role is used only for file-system S3 data operations. A separate mount target, NFS reachability and file access are needed for data use. No full-role credentials or general AWS principal transition follows from PassRole; AWS S3 Files CreateFileSystem docs.

exclusion_technique: Attach a controlled Studio lifecycle configuration to an existing space
Register an Approved model version in a Model Package Group consumed by auto-deploy automation
Replace a mutable ECR image consumed by a later SageMaker Processing job
review_evidence: PutImage on a mutable tag can affect a later Processing job only when the exact future AppSpecification.ImageUri resolves that tag, the image is executable, and the job uses a recorded role with greater authority. Existing processing-job descriptions are historical; they do not prove a pipeline or operator will create another job from the same tag. Candidate for repository/tag, future consumer, execution role and trigger joins.

exclusion_technique: Overwrite S3 code consumed by existing SageMaker training or processing jobs
review_evidence: PutObject can replace an S3 training source bundle or processing input only if the exact configured key is read by a future job and the image actually executes its contents. The current processing projection keeps ImageUri but drops ProcessingInputs; training job facts do not prove a future refresh. Need the exact key, script entrypoint or processing command, trigger, target role and role-readable object. Candidate.

exclusion_technique: Rewrite a notebook-instance lifecycle configuration that runs as the notebook role

review_evidence: GetSchedule returns the configured Target.Input and role ARN, but the input may hold ordinary job data rather than a usable AWS credential. Reading the target role ARN does not grant that role. A principal edge needs the exact schedule, effective GetSchedule permission, a safely identified credential in Input, its AWS subject and additional effective authority; Scheduler GetSchedule API.

exclusion_technique: Run commands or open sessions on hybrid managed nodes that carry an SSM service role
review_evidence: Restored as aws-ssm-sendcommand-hybrid-role and aws-ssm-startsession-hybrid-role in HackTricks Cloud and synced CSPM. Both evaluators bind the same collected online mi- node, its IamRole to the exact IAM role, platform, managed-instance and shell-document grants; the session variant also requires future OpenDataChannel. Positive and wrong node, role, platform, document, channel, offline and denied-inventory negatives pass in tests/test_peaso_privesc_ssm_hybrid_shell.py. AWS InstanceInformation, SSM agent credential precedence and root-level command docs; runtime credential access remains conditional.

exclusion_technique: Re-point an existing hybrid managed node to a passed role
review_evidence: UpdateManagedInstanceRole plus PassRole can change the role of a named existing hybrid node, but returns no credentials to the caller. A principal pivot requires that the caller also control that node or have a verified shell/command route to it, after the role change, with a valid ssm.amazonaws.com-trusting role. The CSPM collects IamRole and PingStatus but has no exact source foothold-to-node join for this route. AWS UpdateManagedInstanceRole and SSM authorization docs.

exclusion_technique: Set the Default Host Management Configuration role to a passed role
review_evidence: UpdateServiceSetting on the exact DHMC service-setting ARN plus PassRole can choose a regional management role, but it does not give the caller that role. A principal pivot also needs an eligible EC2 host the caller can access or command, working IMDSv2 and agent version, and no instance-profile UpdateInstanceInformation permission that takes precedence. Current collector does not join the DHMC setting to eligible controlled hosts. AWS DHMC guide.

exclusion_technique: Resume another user's disconnected Session Manager session
review_evidence: ResumeSession may reconnect an authorized disconnected shell session, but a port-forward or terminated session does not prove node-role access. Need the exact session ARN, its owner restrictions, state, document and managed-node target, plus that node's IAM role and usable data channel. Current CSPM lacks DescribeSessions state/document/target and the session-to-role join. AWS ResumeSession and SSM authorization docs.

SSM for SAP GetDatabase reveals a database credential SecretId, while Secrets Manager GetSecretValue is separately required to retrieve the password. The recovered user is a SAP HANA database identity, not an AWS IAM role; retain as database credential exposure (AWS Systems Manager for SAP guide).

StartAutomationExecution can run an administrator-authored document under a stored assumeRole, but the caller receives neither its credentials nor all of its permissions. A definite authority edge needs the exact document version, literal role, fixed API steps, allowed parameters and source StartAutomationExecution grant, plus a step whose effect exceeds the source's rights. Current CSPM does not collect full runbook content or parameter constraints. AWS Automation runbook and StartAutomationExecution docs.

exclusion_technique: Open an SSM session into an ECS container with ExecuteCommand enabled
review_evidence: AWS documents that direct ssm:StartSession into an ECS Exec-enabled container is possible outside ecs:ExecuteCommand. A definite role edge needs the exact running task, container runtime target ID, ExecuteCommand agent readiness, task role or EC2 fallback role, allowed shell document, StartSession on the task and OpenDataChannel on the new session. Current collector does not retain the runtime target and session readiness join. AWS ECS Exec guide.

exclusion_technique: Modify a custom SSM document already executed by associations or maintenance windows
review_evidence: UpdateDocument and UpdateDocumentDefaultVersion can plant code in a custom document, but an IAM role edge needs a recorded association or maintenance-window task that uses that document's default version on an exact managed node, with a known role and execution schedule or trigger. The collector records document metadata but not enough consumer-to-document and version semantics. Discovery ListDocuments/GetDocument is optional when the name is known. AWS UpdateDocument and State Manager docs.

exclusion_technique: Attach a customer-managed policy reference to a permission set and re-provision it
review_evidence: AttachCustomerManagedPolicyReferenceToPermissionSet plus ProvisionPermissionSet changes assigned roles only where the named/path-matched customer policy exists. Need exact permission set, assigned account, corresponding policy document and effective added rights, plus a user controlled by the source. Candidate; policy name alone cannot prove admin or source reach (AWS Identity Center permission-set provisioning docs).

exclusion_technique: Attach an AWS-managed policy to a permission set and re-provision it
review_evidence: AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet can attach an AWS managed policy such as AdministratorAccess, but an already assigned set needs ProvisionPermissionSet before target roles change. Need exact same set/account, boundary and effective policy evaluation, successful provisioning and source-controlled assigned user/group. Candidate for a direct policy-expansion route (AWS AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet and ProvisionPermissionSet APIs).

exclusion_technique: Assign a permission set to a controlled user in an account
review_evidence: CreateAccountAssignment automatically provisions the selected permission set to the target account, but names an Identity Center USER or GROUP, not the caller IAM principal. Need exact controlled subject, usable portal login, target account/permission set, successful async assignment and resulting role. Candidate; the action grant alone is not role reach (AWS CreateAccountAssignment API).

exclusion_technique: Create an admin permission set and assign it to a controlled user in a member account
review_evidence: The self-contained admin set chain needs CreatePermissionSet, AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet with AdministratorAccess or PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet with effective admin, and CreateAccountAssignment for a source-controlled subject. The assignment auto-provisions a new set, but exact instance, target account, local login/subject and successful async status must be joined. Candidate (AWS CreateAccountAssignment and AttachManagedPolicyToPermissionSet APIs).

exclusion_technique: Reset the password of an Identity Center user
review_evidence: UpdatePassword may give the caller a one-time password for a user in the native Identity Center directory, but external-IdP/AD users are managed elsewhere. Need exact native user, password-reset mode, MFA/login usability, assignments and resulting role. Candidate credential-subject route; a generic UpdatePassword grant cannot prove access to an AWS role (HackTricks Identity Center page; AWS directory API docs).

exclusion_technique: Add an inline policy to a permission set and re-provision it
review_evidence: PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet can replace an inline policy with broader permissions; an assigned set needs ProvisionPermissionSet before its IAM role changes. Need exact set/account, assigned controlled identity, effective policy delta after boundary and SCP, and successful provisioning. Candidate; permission to write the policy by itself does not give the caller that role (AWS ProvisionPermissionSet API).

exclusion_technique: Remove a restricting policy or boundary from a permission set and re-provision it
review_evidence: DeletePermissionsBoundaryFromPermissionSet removes one set-level boundary; it adds no rights if the remaining policies grant nothing beyond the old boundary. Need exact set/account, existing restrictive boundary, effective before/after policy delta, ProvisionPermissionSet and a source-controlled assigned subject. Candidate (AWS DeletePermissionsBoundaryFromPermissionSet and ProvisionPermissionSet APIs).

exclusion_technique: Modify the definition of an existing state machine keeping its role
review_evidence: DescribeStateMachine collection retains exact stateMachineArn, roleArn, status and type; existing pass-role route checks update and start on the same active machine. AWS UpdateStateMachine permits a definition-only update, but Service Authorization Reference lists iam:PassRole as a dependent action; verify whether the unchanged role requires it before restoring a no-PassRole route.

exclusion_technique: Obtain a privileged root-user session in a member account with sts:AssumeRoot
review_evidence: AssumeRoot can issue member-account root credentials only from the Organizations management or IAM delegated-admin account after centralized root sessions are enabled. Every request requires one of five task policies and the session lasts at most 15 minutes; an aws_account_admin edge would overstate it. Candidate bounded root-task permission route needs organization/member/delegation and feature-state joins plus task-policy-specific target authority (AWS AssumeRoot API).

exclusion_technique: Assign Supply Chain application administrator to a controlled Identity Center user
review_evidence: scn:AssignAdminPermissionsToUser assigns an IAM Identity Center user administration of one AWS Supply Chain application. AWS service authorization names the action, but this role is in the Supply Chain web application and does not grant an IAM role, AWS Identity Center permission set or AWS account action. No principal-to-principal AWS IAM escalation is documented; retain as bounded service-plane permission gain.

exclusion_technique: Dry-run replacement canary code under the canary's execution role
review_evidence: AWS StartCanaryDryRun accepts attacker-supplied Code and optional ExecutionRoleArn for an existing canary; DescribeCanaries returns its exact Name and ExecutionRoleArn. This is a principal-to-principal route when the source can perform the dry-run and its Lambda preparation actions on that canary and pass the exact role. CSPM has no synthetics_canary inventory or generated Lambda resource join, so retain exclusion until those fields and composite permissions are checked together. AWS StartCanaryDryRun, DescribeCanaries and service authorization docs.

DescribeConnector identifies a Secrets Manager secret for remote SFTP authentication; GetSecretValue is separately required. Those credentials authenticate to the remote SFTP server, not another AWS IAM principal. Retain as bounded external-service credential exposure (AWS Transfer SFTP connector guide).

UpdateServer or API Gateway response edits select a bounded Transfer file-session role, not general IAM authority. The Lambda UpdateFunctionCode variant can additionally run attacker code under the configured IdP Lambda execution role when Transfer invokes it; the generic Lambda route currently requires direct InvokeFunction and the collector omits IdentityProviderDetails.Function. Need exact server-to-function/role join, active SFTP login trigger and code-signing checks before claiming that IAM role edge. AWS Transfer custom-IdP and Lambda code-signing docs.

ImportSshPublicKey adds a key to a service-managed SFTP user. It can grant bounded S3/EFS file operations through that user, subject to home and session policy, but does not give the source an IAM role session or AWS API credentials. AWS Transfer service-managed user and session-policy guides.

CreateUser/UpdateUser/CreateAccess/UpdateAccess can bind a Transfer-trusting role to an SFTP or directory identity. Authentication uses that role only for Transfer S3/EFS file operations and never gives the caller the role session or unrelated AWS API authority. AWS Transfer user-role and session-policy guides.

Changing the legacy custom-IdP secret may alter a Transfer login and its file-session role, but the returned role is used by Transfer for bounded S3/EFS access. The secret write does not expose or grant the role credentials. AWS Transfer custom-IdP and user-role guides.

A managed Transfer workflow uses the passed role for fixed storage steps or to invoke a separately configured Lambda on an upload. Creating or attaching the workflow does not give its caller that role session or arbitrary API execution. AWS Transfer workflow-execution-role and custom-step guides.

Replacing an AS2 partner signing certificate may cause Transfer to accept partner messages, an application identity and data-integrity issue. It does not grant another AWS IAM principal or its permissions. AWS Transfer AS2 monitoring guide.

An ECS-on-EC2 task may reach the host IMDS role only when the source controls code in that exact task and metadata routing, network mode and host firewall permit it. The current AWS principal graph does not prove a task code foothold or IMDS reachability from it. Candidate for exact task-to-host and network proof, not an IAM grant alone.

A source with root or container-runtime control of a connected ECS host can read co-located task credentials, but host control and actual task placement are runtime facts. ECS inventory records task and container-instance IDs but not source ownership of the host socket or credential endpoint access. Candidate for exact same-host foothold and role join.

The ProcurementPortalSharedSecret belongs to an external procurement integration, not an AWS IAM or STS principal. Reading it or changing the preference may expose or redirect invoice data, but does not give the source another AWS principal. AWS verification and connection testing are separate steps; keep this business-impact route out of the principal escalation graph.

DetachPolicy, UpdatePolicy, DisablePolicyType or MoveAccount from a management/delegated principal can remove a restrictive SCP on an exact member account, but SCPs never grant IAM permission. A principal-to-principal edge requires a separately identified controlled member-account IAM user/role, effective action previously denied solely by that SCP, exact organization hierarchy/attachments and source mutation authority; no escalation for management-account principals (AWS SCP guide).

organizations:PutResourcePolicy from the management account can delegate selected Organizations policy-management actions to a member-account principal. The recipient must also have matching identity-based IAM permissions, and only supported delegated actions/resources are possible. Require exact accepted policy/principal/action/resource, source permission and recipient IAM/guardrail authorization; PutResourcePolicy alone is not usable authority (AWS Organizations delegation guide).

A member account leaving its organization loses its inherited SCP/RCP guardrails, but the caller must be allowed organizations:LeaveOrganization and the account must meet standalone-account prerequisites. The target IAM principal must already have identity/resource authorization blocked by the removed guardrail; no new privilege follows from leaving alone, and organization-path trusts may also cease to work (AWS Organizations/SCP guides).

Deleting or detaching a policy can remove an explicit Deny only when the source is authorized to mutate that exact policy/attachment despite all other denies and boundaries. A verified escalation requires the same controlled target principal, exact statement/attachment, previously blocked action and effective permission after removal; deleting an unrelated policy or a permissions boundary does not establish the delta (AWS IAM policy evaluation and deletion APIs).
